day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 13:00. Take the Magical Express or a budget rideshare (Lyft/Uber) to your boutique stay near Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented. Pick up a Disney park map and review your week's game plan. Visit a nearby Walmart or Publix to stock up on snacks, breakfast items, and water bottles to save money throughout the week.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely stroll along Disney Springs (free admission) to soak in the atmosphere. Browse the shops, enjoy street entertainment, and grab a budget-friendly dinner. Head back early to rest up for the big park days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport or a fast-food spot near the hotel upon arrival — Subway or McDonald's near Lake Buena Vista.
meals.dinner: Disney Springs: Earl of Sandwich for a hearty, affordable sandwich meal (~$10–$13 per person). Great value for a Disney-adjacent dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Focus on settling in, grocery shopping for in-room snacks and breakfasts, and getting a full night's sleep. Buying bottled water and snacks from a grocery store can save $15–$25 per day inside the parks.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom — Early Entry! Arrive at the park gates 30 minutes before official opening (check Disney's early entry benefit if staying on-site). Head straight to Fantasyland: ride Seven Dwarfs Mine Train, Peter Pan's Flight, and The Many Adventures of Winnie the Pooh before crowds build. Then hit Big Thunder Mountain Railroad and Haunted Mansion.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, explore Liberty Square and Adventureland. Ride Pirates of the Caribbean and Jungle Cruise. Cool off with a Dole Whip (a must-try budget treat, ~$6). Watch the Festival of Fantasy Parade in the early afternoon — free and spectacular. Take a mid-afternoon break at the hotel if needed to recharge (especially important in June heat).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Magic Kingdom for the evening. Catch the Main Street Electrical Parade and stay for the Happily Ever After fireworks show over Cinderella Castle — one of the most magical free experiences in all of Disney World. End the night on a high note.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast using groceries purchased on Day 1 (cereal, fruit, granola bars). Save $10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: Cosmic Ray's Starlight Café in Tomorrowland — one of Magic Kingdom's most affordable quick-service spots. Burgers, chicken, and salads around $12–$15 per person.
meals.dinner: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square — clam chowder, fish and chips, or chicken dishes. Budget-friendly quick service, ~$12–$16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Magic Kingdom is the most iconic park — give it a full day. Use Disney's free Lightning Lane planning (if included) wisely. Wear comfortable shoes and bring a refillable water bottle; free water is available at any quick-service counter upon request.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT — arrive at rope drop. Head immediately to World Discovery area: ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (book a virtual queue or Individual Lightning Lane early). Then experience Test Track and Mission: SPACE. These are the most popular rides, so tackle them first thing in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the World Showcase, which opens at 11:00 AM. Walk the 11 pavilions representing different countries — it's essentially a free world tour! Enjoy cultural exhibits, live entertainment, and street performers. Stop at the Canada, UK, France, and Japan pavilions for free shows and architecture. Try one international snack from a food stand as a midday treat.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT's stunning nighttime spectacular — 'EPCOT Forever' or the current evening show over World Showcase Lagoon (free with park admission). Dine in the World Showcase for a memorable budget dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — yogurt, fruit, and granola bars from your grocery haul.
meals.lunch: Sunshine Seasons in The Land pavilion — one of EPCOT's best value quick-service spots. Fresh sandwiches, grain bowls, and Asian-inspired dishes for ~$12–$15.
meals.dinner: Yorkshire County Fish Shop (UK Pavilion) — classic fish and chips for ~$10–$12. Affordable, delicious, and a fun cultural experience.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is walkable and culturally rich — perfect for families who love entertainment and exploration. The World Showcase is free to walk and full of live music and performances. Hydration is critical in June; refill water bottles at any quick-service location for free.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios — arrive at rope drop. Sprint to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge first. Ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run (standby line is often shorter at opening). If time permits, try to get a boarding group for Rise of the Resistance — one of the most immersive rides ever built. Then head to Toy Story Land: Slinky Dog Dash and Toy Story Mania are great for all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular (free show with park admission — a must-see!). Explore Hollywood Boulevard and Echo Lake. Ride Rock 'n' Roller Coaster and The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror for thrill seekers. Take a mid-afternoon break in an air-conditioned show: Muppet*Vision 3D is fun and gives your feet a rest.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the Fantasmic! nighttime show — a spectacular outdoor water, fire, and projection show featuring Mickey Mouse battling Disney villains. This is one of Disney's best free evening experiences. Grab a quick dinner before the show to secure good seating.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — peanut butter on bread, fruit, and juice boxes.
meals.lunch: Woody's Lunch Box in Toy Story Land — affordable and themed. Grilled cheese, BBQ brisket melts, and lemonade for ~$10–$13 per item.
meals.dinner: ABC Commissary — one of Hollywood Studios' most budget-friendly quick-service spots. Burgers, chicken sandwiches, and wraps for ~$12–$15.

day_by_day.notes: Hollywood Studios is action-packed. June crowds can be heavy — prioritize your must-do rides in the first two hours. The Fantasmic! show requires arriving 30–45 minutes early for good standing spots; bring a small blanket or towel to sit on.

day_by_day.morning: Animal Kingdom — arrive at rope drop. Head directly to Pandora – The World of Avatar. Ride Avatar Flight of Passage (the park's most popular attraction — lines can exceed 2 hours by mid-morning). Then ride Na'vi River Journey for a more relaxed experience. Pandora is breathtaking in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Africa and Asia sections of the park. Ride Kilimanjaro Safaris (best in the morning or late afternoon when animals are most active — consider a second ride if time allows). Watch the Festival of the Lion King show — a Broadway-quality performance included with park admission. Walk the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail for free wildlife viewing.
day_by_day.evening: Animal Kingdom typically closes earlier than other parks. Head back to Disney Springs for a relaxed evening of free entertainment, live music on the waterfront, and an affordable dinner. Browse the LEGO store and other shops for fun without pressure to buy.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — cereal, milk, and bananas.
meals.lunch: Flame Tree Barbecue in Discovery Island — one of Disney World's best quick-service meals. Ribs, pulled pork, and chicken for ~$13–$17. Eat at the outdoor waterfront seating area for a beautiful view.
meals.dinner: Disney Springs: Blaze Pizza — build-your-own artisan pizza for ~$9–$12. Fast, affordable, and delicious. Great family option.

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom's Pandora area is stunning at night with bioluminescent lighting, but the park often closes by 8–9 PM. Plan accordingly. The Kilimanjaro Safaris is free with admission and genuinely world-class wildlife viewing — don't skip it.

day_by_day.morning: Flex/Revisit Day — Return to your favorite park from earlier in the week to catch any rides or shows you missed. Alternatively, spend the morning at the hotel pool (free amenity) for a relaxing break — especially valuable for families with young children who may be experiencing theme park fatigue by Day 6.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free resort areas around Magic Kingdom. Take the complimentary Disney monorail loop (no park ticket required from the Transportation and Ticket Center) for a scenic ride past the Grand Floridian, Polynesian, and Contemporary resorts. Walk through the resort lobbies — they're beautifully themed and free to explore. Visit the Polynesian Village Resort beach for a stunning view of Cinderella Castle across Seven Seas Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Magic Kingdom for a final evening visit. Focus on anything you missed on Day 2 — especially rides with shorter evening wait times. Stay for the nighttime fireworks one more time; they never get old. This is your last big park evening, so make it memorable.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — use remaining grocery items. Toast, eggs (if you have a microwave/mini kitchen), and fruit.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic-style lunch using grocery store snacks and sandwiches made in-room. Eat at the Polynesian resort beach or a park picnic area to save money.
meals.dinner: Magic Kingdom: Pecos Bill Tall Tale Inn & Café — Tex-Mex quick service with a legendary free toppings bar. Burgers, tacos, and nachos for ~$12–$15. The toppings bar (rice, beans, salsa, cheese) makes it exceptional value.

day_by_day.notes: Day 6 is intentionally flexible — use it to rest, revisit favorites, or explore free Disney resort areas. The monorail resort loop is a hidden gem that most budget travelers overlook. It's a magical, free experience that gives you a behind-the-scenes feel of Disney's most iconic hotels.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final in-room breakfast. Check out of the hotel per the checkout time (typically 11:00 AM). Store luggage at the front desk if your flight is later in the day. Take one last walk through the Disney Springs area if time allows — pick up any souvenirs you've been eyeing all week. Disney Springs has free parking and no admission fee, making it the perfect last stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your flight time, head to Orlando International Airport with plenty of time (allow 2+ hours before departure). Take a rideshare (Lyft/Uber, ~$25–$35) or Disney's Magical Express if available. Reflect on an incredible week of memories!
day_by_day.evening: Travel home. If your flight is an evening departure, enjoy a final meal at the airport or a nearby restaurant before heading through security.

meals.breakfast: Final in-room breakfast — finish off remaining groceries (granola bars, fruit, juice). Zero waste, maximum savings.
meals.lunch: Disney Springs: Wolfgang Puck Express — slightly more upscale but still reasonable at ~$14–$18. A nice treat to celebrate the end of a fantastic trip.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Budget tip recap for the week: Buying groceries on Day 1 for in-room breakfasts saves approximately $70–$100 for a family of four over 7 days. Always request free ice water at quick-service restaurants. Use Disney's free entertainment (parades, fireworks, shows) to maximize value. Total estimated park spending per adult: $400–$500 for 5-day park tickets if purchased in advance online. Look for multi-day ticket discounts on Disney's official website or through AAA/military discounts.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Travel from Orlando International Airport to your Boutique Stay near Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista. Use Disney's Magical Express or a rideshare (~30–45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort map and park apps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disney Springs Exploration — Head to Disney Springs (free admission, no park ticket needed) for a relaxed first afternoon. Browse the shops, visit the LEGO Store, check out the World of Disney flagship store, and soak in the atmosphere. Pick up any last-minute supplies or souvenirs. Great low-key introduction to the Disney universe after a long travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Disney Springs Dining & Entertainment Evening — Stay at Disney Springs for dinner and evening entertainment. Watch street performers, enjoy live music at the Waterfront stage, and browse the entertainment venues. Wind down and get to bed early to prepare for full park days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Grab something light at the airport or on the plane before landing.
meals.lunch: D-Luxe Burger at Disney Springs — casual, mid-range, quick-service burgers and shakes (~$15–$20 per person).
meals.dinner: The BOATHOUSE at Disney Springs — waterfront dining with seafood, steaks, and classic American fare. Mid-range splurge for arrival night (~$35–$55 per person). Reservations recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Download the My Disney Experience app before arrival. Link your park tickets and hotel reservation. Set up Disney MagicMobile on your phone. Purchase Lightning Lane passes in advance if desired. Stay hydrated — Orlando in June is hot and humid (expect 90°F / 32°C+). Disney Springs requires no park ticket and is a perfect soft landing for Day 1.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom — Early Entry & Iconic Rides — Arrive at Magic Kingdom at park opening (or use Early Theme Park Entry benefit if staying on-site, typically 30 min early). Head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain, then Fantasyland for Seven Dwarfs Mine Train (use Lightning Lane if available). Ride Peter Pan's Flight and It's a Small World before crowds build. Explore Main Street U.S.A. and grab a classic photo in front of Cinderella Castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Magic Kingdom — Adventureland & Liberty Square — After lunch, tackle Pirates of the Caribbean, Jungle Cruise, and Haunted Mansion. Watch the Festival of Fantasy Parade (check daily schedule). Take a mid-afternoon break back at the hotel during peak heat (2–4 PM) if needed, then return refreshed for the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Magic Kingdom — Nighttime Spectacular — Return to Magic Kingdom for the iconic Happily Ever After fireworks show or Disney Enchantment nighttime spectacular (check current show schedule for 2027). Grab a prime spot on Main Street U.S.A. 30–45 minutes early. End the night with a Mickey-shaped ice cream bar.

meals.breakfast: The Wave… of American Flavors at Disney's Contemporary Resort — healthy, farm-to-table breakfast options, walkable from Magic Kingdom (~$20–$30 per person). Alternatively, grab a quick pastry on Main Street U.S.A.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square — quick-service seafood and sandwiches inside Magic Kingdom (~$15–$20 per person). Shaded indoor seating — great midday refuge from the heat.
meals.dinner: Be Our Guest Restaurant in Fantasyland — dine inside the Beast's enchanted castle. Prix-fixe dinner with French-inspired dishes (~$60–$75 per person). Book well in advance. Magical atmosphere worth the splurge.

day_by_day.notes: Magic Kingdom is typically the most crowded park — arrive early and use Lightning Lane strategically. Wear comfortable shoes and bring sunscreen, hats, and a refillable water bottle. Check the My Disney Experience app for real-time wait times. Lockers are available near the park entrance if you need to store items during the midday hotel break.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT — Future World & Guardians of the Galaxy — Arrive at EPCOT at opening. Use Early Entry to ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue or Lightning Lane — secure your spot immediately upon park opening). Then experience Remy's Ratatouille Adventure in the France Pavilion and Test Track. Visit Mission: SPACE for a thrilling astronaut simulation.
day_by_day.afternoon: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour — Spend the afternoon strolling the World Showcase Lagoon. Sample dishes and drinks from pavilions representing Mexico, Norway, China, Germany, Italy, America, Japan, Morocco, France, United Kingdom, and Canada. Try the famous Norwegian School Bread, Mexican street corn, Japanese sushi rolls, and French crepes. Catch a live cultural performance in one of the pavilions.
day_by_day.evening: EPCOT — EPCOT Forever or Harmonious Nighttime Show — End the day at the World Showcase Lagoon for EPCOT's nighttime spectacular (confirm show name for 2027 season). Find a spot near the American Adventure pavilion for the best views. Enjoy one final World Showcase treat before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Sunshine Seasons in The Land Pavilion, EPCOT — quick-service with fresh, healthy options including grain bowls, sandwiches, and fresh-squeezed juices (~$12–$18 per person).
meals.lunch: World Showcase grazing — budget $20–$30 per person for small plates and snacks across multiple pavilions. Highlights: Kringla Bakeri Og Kafé (Norway), Lotus Blossom Café (China), and Tutto Gusto Wine Cellar (Italy).
meals.dinner: Teppan Edo in the Japan Pavilion — hibachi-style teppanyaki dining with skilled chefs cooking at your table. Fun, interactive, and mid-range (~$35–$55 per person). Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT's World Showcase officially opens at noon, but Future World attractions open at park open. Plan Future World rides in the morning and World Showcase in the afternoon and evening. The EPCOT Food & Wine Festival runs seasonally — check if it overlaps with your June visit for extra food booths and live music. Comfortable walking shoes are essential as EPCOT requires significant walking.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios — Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge — Arrive at Hollywood Studios at early entry time. Head directly to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge in Batuu. Ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run first (walk-on or Lightning Lane). Experience Rise of the Resistance — one of Disney's most immersive attractions (Lightning Lane highly recommended). Explore the land: interact with droids, sip blue or green milk from the Milk Stand, and browse Dok-Ondar's Den of Antiquities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Savi's Workshop — Build a Custom Lightsaber & More Hollywood Studios — Book a lightsaber-building experience at Savi's Workshop (approximately $299.99 per lightsaber — reserve well in advance, limited slots). While one family member builds, others can ride Slinky Dog Dash in Toy Story Land or Tower of Terror. Catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular show (check schedule).
day_by_day.evening: Hollywood Studios — Fantasmic! & Sunset Boulevard — Watch Fantasmic!, Hollywood Studios' legendary nighttime water, fire, and projection show at the Hollywood Hills Amphitheater (check 2027 schedule for show times). Grab a spot 45–60 minutes early. End the night with a stroll down Sunset Boulevard.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at your hotel before heading to the park, or pick up a pastry at Trolley Car Café on Hollywood Blvd inside the park (~$8–$12).
meals.lunch: Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo in Galaxy's Edge — Star Wars-themed quick-service with unique dishes like Smoked Kaadu Ribs and Fried Endorian Tip-Yip (~$18–$25 per person). Fully immersive theming.
meals.dinner: 50's Prime Time Café at Hollywood Studios — retro 1950s diner atmosphere with classic American comfort food like pot roast, fried chicken, and milkshakes (~$25–$40 per person). Fun, kitschy, and family-friendly.

day_by_day.notes: Savi's Workshop reservations are mandatory and sell out months in advance — book as soon as your trip is confirmed. Droid Depot (build your own droid, ~$119.99) is an alternative or addition for Star Wars fans. Hollywood Studios tends to have high crowd levels — Lightning Lane Multi Pass is strongly recommended for this park. Wear comfortable shoes; the park is large.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Animal Kingdom — Kilimanjaro Safari & Avatar: Flight of Passage — Arrive at Animal Kingdom at early entry. Rush to Pandora – The World of Avatar for Avatar: Flight of Passage (Lightning Lane strongly recommended — this is one of Disney's most in-demand rides). Then experience Na'vi River Journey for a gentler float through bioluminescent rainforest. Head to Africa for the Kilimanjaro Safari — best in the morning when animals are most active. Spot lions, elephants, giraffes, hippos, and more on the 18-minute open-vehicle safari.
day_by_day.afternoon: Animal Kingdom — Expedition Everest & Conservation Station — Ride Expedition Everest in Asia (thrilling roller coaster through the Himalayas). Visit the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail and Maharajah Jungle Trek for up-close wildlife encounters. Stop by Conservation Station at Rafiki's Planet Watch to meet animal care experts and see behind-the-scenes conservation work. Take the Wildlife Express Train to get there.
day_by_day.evening: Tree of Life Awakening & Rivers of Light — As sunset approaches, find a spot near the Tree of Life to watch the magical Tree of Life Awakening projections (shown throughout the evening on the hour). If Rivers of Light or a nighttime show is scheduled for 2027, grab seats early. Animal Kingdom typically has an earlier closing time — plan to wrap up by park close and enjoy a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at your hotel or pick up a quick snack at Harambe Market when it opens in the park (~$10–$15).
meals.lunch: Flame Tree Barbecue in Discovery Island — open-air quick-service with smoked ribs, pulled pork, and chicken with beautiful waterfront seating (~$18–$25 per person). One of the best quick-service spots in all of Walt Disney World.
meals.dinner: Yak & Yeti Restaurant in Asia — pan-Asian cuisine including Ahi tuna nachos, Peking duck, and mango pie. Sit-down mid-range dining (~$25–$45 per person). Great atmosphere with Himalayan décor.

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom often has the earliest park closing time among the four parks — check the 2027 schedule. The safari experience is weather-dependent; animals may be less visible during extreme heat midday, reinforcing the morning visit strategy. June heat in Florida can be intense — the shaded jungle trails at Animal Kingdom provide some relief. Bring bug spray for outdoor trail areas.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom — Second Visit for Missed Attractions & Character Meets — Return to Magic Kingdom for any rides or experiences missed on Day 2. Target: Big Thunder Mountain Railroad, Splash Mountain (check if operational in 2027), Tomorrowland Speedway, or Buzz Lightyear's Space Ranger Spin. Book a character dining breakfast or a meet-and-greet with Mickey, Minnie, or princesses at Town Square Theater.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort Pool & Relaxation Day — Take a well-deserved mid-trip rest. Spend the afternoon at your boutique hotel's pool or explore the resort grounds. Many Disney-area hotels have themed pools, waterslides, and recreational activities. This is a great time to recharge, do laundry, review photos, and let kids have unstructured play time. Alternatively, visit Disney's Typhoon Lagoon or Blizzard Beach water park (separate ticket required) for a cool afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: EPCOT — Return Visit for Any Missed Pavilions or Dining — Head back to EPCOT in the evening for a relaxed World Showcase stroll. Visit any pavilions missed on Day 3, shop for international souvenirs, and enjoy one more nighttime spectacular viewing from a different vantage point around the lagoon.

meals.breakfast: Chef Mickey's at Disney's Contemporary Resort — beloved character dining buffet with Mickey, Minnie, Donald, Goofy, and Pluto. Full American breakfast buffet (~$45–$60 per person). Book months in advance. Iconic Disney experience.
meals.lunch: Pool-side or hotel dining — casual burgers, sandwiches, or a resort quick-service option (~$15–$20 per person). Relax and enjoy the resort.
meals.dinner: La Hacienda de San Angel at EPCOT's Mexico Pavilion — waterfront table-service restaurant with authentic Mexican cuisine and views of the World Showcase Lagoon. Perfect for watching the nighttime show from your table (~$35–$55 per person). Reserve a lagoon-view table in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is typically one of the busiest days at Walt Disney World — the afternoon resort break is strategically timed to avoid peak afternoon crowds. If visiting a water park, check height restrictions for children and bring water shoes, sunscreen, and towels. The EPCOT evening visit benefits from lighter crowds as many day visitors depart. This balanced day prevents park fatigue heading into the final full day.

day_by_day.morning: Final Park Choice — Hollywood Studios or EPCOT Deep Dive — Choose based on family preference and any remaining must-dos. Option A: Return to Hollywood Studios for Star Tours, Alien Swirling Saucers in Toy Story Land, Muppet*Vision 3D, and a second ride on any favorites. Option B: EPCOT for any Future World attractions not yet experienced, such as Soarin' Around the World, Living with the Land boat ride, and the Seas with Nemo & Friends. Use the morning for maximum ride efficiency before crowds peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disney Springs — Final Shopping & Farewell — Spend the final afternoon at Disney Springs for last-minute souvenir shopping. Visit the World of Disney store for gifts, stop by the Disney Style store for apparel, and browse specialty shops like Marketplace Co-Op. Pick up Mickey ears, character merchandise, and Florida-exclusive items. Relax at the waterfront with a final Disney treat.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner at Disney Springs & Hotel Wind-Down — Enjoy a memorable farewell dinner at Disney Springs. Return to the hotel to pack, review your trip memories, and prepare for departure. If flying out the next morning, confirm transportation to Orlando International Airport.

meals.breakfast: Kona Café at Disney's Polynesian Village Resort — beloved breakfast spot with Tonga Toast (banana-stuffed sourdough French toast), macadamia nut pancakes, and tropical drinks (~$20–$30 per person). A Disney institution worth the short trip.
meals.lunch: Quick-service at your final park — grab a favorite from earlier in the trip or try something new. Budget $15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: STK Orlando at Disney Springs — upscale-casual modern steakhouse with a lively atmosphere. Enjoy premium cuts, creative sides, and craft cocktails for a celebratory farewell meal (~$50–$80 per person). Reserve in advance. Alternatively, Paddlefish (seafood) or The Edison (American industrial) offer similar mid-to-upscale options at Disney Springs.

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is on June 22, confirm checkout time with your boutique hotel and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late flight. Disney's Resort Airline Check-In service (if available in 2027) allows you to check bags and receive boarding passes at select Disney resort hotels — confirm availability. Take a final walk through your favorite park area or along the Magic Kingdom ferry dock at sunset for a magical send-off. Don't forget to back up all your photos before leaving!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

experiences.name: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Magic Kingdom with classic rides like Space Mountain, Pirates of the Caribbean, and the Haunted Mansion. Watch the spectacular Festival of Fantasy parade and end the night with the breathtaking Happily Ever After fireworks show over Cinderella Castle.
experiences.location: Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

experiences.name: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour
experiences.description: Stroll through EPCOT's World Showcase and sample authentic cuisines from 11 countries including Japan, Morocco, France, and Mexico. Enjoy cultural performances, artisan demonstrations, and unique pavilion-exclusive merchandise while experiencing global cultures without leaving Florida.
experiences.location: EPCOT World Showcase, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

experiences.name: Hollywood Studios Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure
experiences.description: Immerse your family in the Star Wars universe at Batuu. Build a custom lightsaber at Savi's Workshop, pilot the Millennium Falcon on Smugglers Run, and experience the thrilling Rise of the Resistance ride. Dine at the Oga's Cantina for themed drinks and snacks.
experiences.location: Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge, Hollywood Studios, Orlando

experiences.name: Disney's Animal Kingdom Safari & Avatar Experience
experiences.description: Embark on the Kilimanjaro Safari to see real African wildlife including lions, elephants, and giraffes. Then journey to Pandora – The World of Avatar for the stunning Flight of Passage ride and the Na'vi River Journey. The park's lush landscapes make it a unique blend of nature and fantasy.
experiences.location: Disney's Animal Kingdom, Bay Lake, Orlando

experiences.name: Disney Springs Dining & Entertainment Evening
experiences.description: Spend a free-admission evening at Disney Springs exploring over 60 restaurants, shops, and entertainment venues. Enjoy a family dinner at T-REX Cafe surrounded by animatronic dinosaurs, catch a live street performance, and browse unique Disney merchandise and third-party boutiques along the waterfront.
experiences.location: Disney Springs, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Resort Check-In: Flight LH lands at 13:00, so morning is in transit. Arrange a pre-booked Disney Magical Express or private luxury transfer from Orlando International Airport to your boutique stay at Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista. No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort Orientation & Magic Kingdom First Look: After check-in, take a leisurely stroll along the monorail loop or a private resort boat to Magic Kingdom's main gate. Enjoy a relaxed first look at Cinderella Castle, grab a Mickey Premium Bar, and explore Main Street U.S.A. at your own pace. Book Lightning Lane Individual selections for Space Mountain or Seven Dwarfs Mine Train via the Disney app for a late-afternoon ride.
day_by_day.evening: Magic Kingdom Park – Wishes & Fireworks Night: Stay for the 'Disney Enchantment' or 'Happily Ever After' nighttime spectacular over Cinderella Castle. Secure a premium reserved fireworks viewing package through Disney's dessert party add-on for guaranteed front-row views with exclusive desserts and beverages included.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or grab a light snack at the airport lounge (Amex Centurion Lounge, MCO) before landing.
meals.lunch: Be Our Guest Restaurant (Magic Kingdom) – Reserve the quick-service lunch for an immersive Beauty and the Beast themed dining experience inside Cinderella Castle's West Wing.
meals.dinner: Cinderella's Royal Table – A signature Disney dining experience inside Cinderella Castle. Enjoy a prix-fixe menu with character meet-and-greets. Book 60 days in advance. Dress code: smart casual.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book all dining reservations 60 days out via My Disney Experience. Purchase Genie+ and Lightning Lane selections at 7:00 AM on the day of your park visit. Confirm private airport transfer 48 hours before arrival. Request early check-in through the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day – Rope Drop: Arrive at Magic Kingdom 30 minutes before park opening for 'Early Theme Park Entry' (exclusive to Disney resort guests, 30 minutes early access). Prioritize Seven Dwarfs Mine Train, Tiana's Bayou Adventure, and Peter Pan's Flight before crowds build. Use Lightning Lane Multi Pass for additional ride access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Magic Kingdom Continued – Classic Attractions & Character Experiences: Enjoy Pirates of the Caribbean, Haunted Mansion, and Space Mountain. Visit the Harmony Barber Shop on Main Street U.S.A. for a fun pixie-dust hair experience (book in advance). Cool off with a Dole Whip float at Aloha Isle.
day_by_day.evening: Magic Kingdom – Festival of Fantasy Parade & Evening Rides: Catch the Festival of Fantasy afternoon parade, then revisit favorite attractions with shorter evening wait times. End the night watching the 'Disney Enchantment' fireworks spectacular from the premium reserved dessert party viewing area on the Tomorrowland Terrace.

meals.breakfast: The Contemporary Resort's Chef Mickey's – A beloved character breakfast buffet featuring Mickey, Minnie, Donald, Goofy, and Pluto. Accessible by monorail from your resort.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House (Magic Kingdom) – Elevated quick-service with New England-inspired seafood options including lobster rolls and clam chowder.
meals.dinner: The Wave… of American Flavors (Disney's Contemporary Resort) – A sophisticated farm-to-table dinner with locally sourced ingredients, craft cocktails, and a serene ambiance just steps from Magic Kingdom via monorail.

day_by_day.notes: Full Magic Kingdom day. Wear comfortable shoes and bring a portable fan or cooling towel for June heat. Download the My Disney Experience app to monitor wait times and Lightning Lane availability in real time. Stay hydrated — free water cups are available at any quick-service location.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour – Morning Arrival: Take the monorail or Disney Skyliner to EPCOT. Begin with Future World (now 'World Discovery' and 'World Nature') early — ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue or Lightning Lane Individual) and Test Track. Explore the stunning 'Living with the Land' boat ride.
day_by_day.afternoon: EPCOT World Showcase Culinary Journey: Begin the World Showcase loop at 11:00 AM. Sample authentic cuisines and beverages from Japan (sushi, sake), France (crêpes, macarons), Morocco, Italy, and Mexico. Participate in the EPCOT International Food & Wine Festival activities if running in June. Visit the France Pavilion's Remy's Ratatouille Adventure ride (Lightning Lane recommended).
day_by_day.evening: EPCOT – EPCOT Forever or Harmonious Nighttime Spectacular: Stay for EPCOT's signature nighttime lagoon show featuring fireworks, illuminated kites, and water screens. Enjoy a farewell drink at La Cava del Tequila (Mexico Pavilion) before heading back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Katsura Grill or a continental spread at your resort before departing — or grab a croissant and café au lait at Les Halles Boulangerie-Patisserie (France Pavilion, EPCOT) upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Teppan Edo (Japan Pavilion, EPCOT) – A premium hibachi-style teppanyaki dining experience with skilled chefs preparing steak, seafood, and vegetables tableside. Reserve 60 days in advance.
meals.dinner: Monsieur Paul (France Pavilion, EPCOT) – EPCOT's most refined dining destination. A classic French fine-dining restaurant inspired by the legendary chef Paul Bocuse. Offers a prix-fixe menu with wine pairings. Jacket optional but smart attire recommended.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is expansive — wear comfortable walking shoes. The World Showcase doesn't open until 11:00 AM, so plan Future World attractions in the morning. Consider the EPCOT International Gateway entrance (near France and UK Pavilions) for direct Skyliner access from select resorts. Book Teppan Edo and Monsieur Paul well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios – Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure: Use Early Theme Park Entry to head straight to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge at Batuu. First priority: Rise of the Resistance (Lightning Lane Individual — purchase at 7:00 AM sharp). Then experience Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run. Soak in the immersive theming of Black Spire Outpost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hollywood Studios – Savi's Workshop & Galaxy's Edge Exploration: Book the premium Savi's Workshop experience to build a custom lightsaber ($300+ per saber, reservations required months in advance). Visit Droid Depot to build a custom droid. Explore Oga's Cantina for exotic themed cocktails and snacks (reservations required). Also enjoy Toy Story Land: Slinky Dog Dash and Alien Swirling Saucers.
day_by_day.evening: Hollywood Studios – Fantasmic! & Tower of Terror: Watch the spectacular 'Fantasmic!' nighttime show at the Hollywood Hills Amphitheater — book the Fantasmic! Dining Package for guaranteed reserved seating. End the night with a thrilling ride on The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster Starring Aerosmith.

meals.breakfast: Woody's Lunch Box (Toy Story Land, Hollywood Studios) – A charming quick-service spot with hearty breakfast totchos, lunch box tarts, and specialty lemonades.
meals.lunch: Oga's Cantina (Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge) – Sip on themed cocktails like the Fuzzy Tauntaun or Jedi Mind Trick alongside light bites in this immersive bar. Reservations are essential.
meals.dinner: Hollywood Brown Derby (Hollywood Studios) – A recreation of the legendary 1930s Hollywood hotspot. Signature dishes include the Cobb Salad (invented at the original Brown Derby) and pan-seared grouper. An elegant, character-inspired fine-dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Savi's Workshop reservations are extremely limited and sell out quickly — book as soon as the 60-day window opens. Rise of the Resistance Lightning Lane Individual must be purchased at exactly 7:00 AM on the day of your visit. The Fantasmic! Dining Package includes reserved show seating — book at 60 days.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Animal Kingdom – Kilimanjaro Safari & Avatar Experience: Use Early Entry to head straight to Pandora – The World of Avatar. Ride Avatar Flight of Passage (Lightning Lane Individual — purchase at 7:00 AM) before crowds arrive. Follow with Na'vi River Journey for a serene, immersive experience through bioluminescent rainforest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Animal Kingdom – Kilimanjaro Safari & Wildlife Exploration: Board the Kilimanjaro Safari for a 20-minute open-air adventure through 110 acres of authentic African savanna, spotting lions, elephants, giraffes, zebras, and rhinos. Visit the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail and Maharajah Jungle Trek for up-close wildlife encounters. Catch the 'Festival of the Lion King' live stage show — one of Disney's best theatrical productions.
day_by_day.evening: Animal Kingdom – Rivers of Light & Tree of Life Awakening: As dusk falls, witness the Tree of Life 'Awakenings' — a stunning projection show where the tree comes alive with animal spirits. Enjoy a peaceful evening stroll through Discovery Island before heading back to the resort for a relaxing night.

meals.breakfast: Satu'li Canteen (Pandora, Animal Kingdom) – A visually stunning quick-service restaurant serving hearty bowls with grains, proteins, and signature sauces inspired by Pandoran cuisine. Excellent for a filling morning meal.
meals.lunch: Tiffins Restaurant (Animal Kingdom) – Disney's most sophisticated Animal Kingdom dining experience. A signature restaurant celebrating the art of travel and exploration, featuring globally inspired dishes like braised short rib, whole-fried sustainable fish, and artisan charcuterie. Reserve 60 days in advance.
meals.dinner: Jiko – The Cooking Place (Disney's Animal Kingdom Lodge) – One of Walt Disney World's most acclaimed fine-dining restaurants. Features African, Indian, and Mediterranean-inspired cuisine with an award-winning all-African wine list. Take a resort shuttle or Minnie Van service to Animal Kingdom Lodge.

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom is best experienced in the morning when animals are most active on the safari. June heat peaks in the afternoon — plan a midday resort break if needed. Tiffins Restaurant is a hidden gem and considered one of the best restaurants on Disney property. Book Jiko at 60 days — it's a top-tier experience worth the trip to Animal Kingdom Lodge.

day_by_day.morning: Disney Springs – Leisure Morning & Boutique Shopping: Enjoy a relaxed morning sleeping in or using the resort's luxury pool facilities. Head to Disney Springs mid-morning for world-class shopping at boutiques including Anthropologie, UNIQLO, Pandora, and the massive World of Disney store. Browse unique Disney art at the Marketplace Co-Op.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disney Springs – Entertainment & Exploration: Visit the NBA Experience for interactive basketball activities. Explore the LEGO Store's massive outdoor display. Catch a matinee at the AMC Disney Springs 24 Theatre (IMAX available). Browse the Coca-Cola Store's rooftop tasting bar or the Splitsville Luxury Lanes for upscale bowling and entertainment.
day_by_day.evening: Disney Springs Dining & Entertainment Evening: Enjoy the vibrant evening atmosphere at Disney Springs. Watch live performers and street entertainment. Explore the waterfront promenade and enjoy a nightcap at Jock Lindsey's Hangar Bar — an Indiana Jones-themed cocktail lounge with creative drinks and light bites.

meals.breakfast: The Boathouse (Disney Springs) – A waterfront dining gem offering a premium brunch with eggs Benedict, lobster omelettes, fresh-squeezed juices, and mimosas. Enjoy views of the marina and vintage amphicars.
meals.lunch: STK Orlando (Disney Springs) – A trendy, upscale steakhouse with a lively atmosphere. Features USDA Prime steaks, truffle fries, and creative cocktails. Perfect for a luxurious midday indulgence.
meals.dinner: Morimoto Asia (Disney Springs) – Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto's flagship Disney restaurant. An expansive, dramatic space serving Pan-Asian cuisine including Peking duck, sushi, dim sum, and Morimoto's signature ramen. An exceptional fine-dining experience with an impressive sake and cocktail list.

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs is free to enter with no park ticket required — perfect for a relaxed day. Amphicar boat tours are available at The BOATHOUSE for a unique 20-minute water excursion ($125 per car). Disney Springs can get crowded on Saturday evenings — arrive for dinner reservations early. Valet parking is available for resort guests using personal or Minnie Van transportation.

day_by_day.morning: Final Park Day – EPCOT or Magic Kingdom Revisit: Choose your favorite park for a final morning farewell. Magic Kingdom is ideal for any missed attractions or a sentimental last walk down Main Street U.S.A. Alternatively, return to EPCOT for any World Showcase pavilions not yet explored. Use remaining Lightning Lane selections wisely.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort Relaxation & Farewell Experience: Return to the resort for a final afternoon of luxury. Enjoy the resort pool, book a spa treatment at a nearby Disney resort spa (Senses Spa at Disney's Grand Floridian or Saratoga Springs), or take a private guided tour of the resort grounds. Pack and prepare for departure. Arrange private luxury transfer to Orlando International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure Preparation & Farewell Dinner: Enjoy a final, memorable dinner before heading to the airport or resting at the resort for an early next-day departure. Reflect on an extraordinary week at the most magical place on Earth.

meals.breakfast: Grand Floridian Café (Disney's Grand Floridian Resort) – An elegant, Victorian-inspired breakfast featuring eggs Florentine, lemon ricotta pancakes, and fresh-pressed juices. Accessible by monorail — a wonderful final morning treat.
meals.lunch: Coral Reef Restaurant (EPCOT, The Seas Pavilion) – Dine alongside a 5.7-million-gallon aquarium teeming with marine life. Enjoy sustainable seafood, chowder, and premium entrées with an unforgettable underwater view.
meals.dinner: Victoria & Albert's (Disney's Grand Floridian Resort & Spa) – Walt Disney World's only AAA Five Diamond restaurant and one of the finest dining experiences in the United States. An intimate, prix-fixe tasting menu (10+ courses) with optional wine pairings and tableside preparations. Jacket required for gentlemen. Reserve 60 days in advance — this is the pinnacle of Disney dining.

day_by_day.notes: Victoria & Albert's is the crown jewel of Disney dining — require formal attire, no children under 10, and is one of the hardest reservations to secure on Disney property. Book at exactly the 60-day mark. For departure, Disney's Magical Express or a private Minnie Van service can transfer you to MCO. Check luggage with resort airline check-in (Resort Airline Check-In service) if available to streamline your airport experience. Allow 3+ hours before international departure flights.

query: Disney World Orlando family of 4, $6000, 7 days, June 2026
